$(cat:
Korax (Κόραξ) — the Crow

Core concept
- A recurring trickster “enemy” who creates gentle, fixable problems. Clever, curious, and proud, Korax loves shiny things and attention. He teases, tests boundaries, and sometimes takes what isn’t his, but he is never cruel or scary. Conflicts end with repair, trade, sharing, or learning.

Role in the series
- Antagonist/foil who drives small, everyday conflicts (missing spoon, noisy interruptions, shiny-object heists) that resolve through kindness, patience, and clear choices.
- Serves as a fun source of repetition and high‑frequency Koine verbs (sees, wants, takes, brings, gives, goes, says, hears) and simple questions.
- A bridge from mischief to community: over books, he learns to ask first, trade fairly, and help when it matters.

Personality
- Quick-witted, bold, opportunistic; easily distracted by anything bright or tasty.
- Playful show‑off; enjoys being watched and hearing his own voice.
- Not mean—just pushy and proud. Embarrassed when caught; secretly likes being included.

Motivations
- Shiny things, crunchy snacks, and being the center of attention.
- Curiosity about what the children are doing; desire to join without admitting it.

Signature behaviors
- Hops, tilts head, flicks tail, sidesteps; sudden swoops are short and low.
- Stashes finds in a familiar spot: a hollow stump near the creek (use this consistently across titles).
- Mimics short Greek words and sounds; caws to announce himself.
- When offered a fair trade, he returns or shares what he took.

Voice and sounds
- Catch cry: κρα, κρα! (use as onomatopoeia on pages).
- Frequently repeats last words he hears; short, rhythmic lines work best.
- Sample simple lines for writers: ὁ Κόραξ βλέπει. ὁ Κόραξ θέλει. λαμβάνει τὸ λαμπρόν. φέρει πάλιν. δίδωσι; λέγει· κρα, κρα!

Language focus (for writers)
- High‑frequency present‑tense verbs: βλέπει, θέλει, λαμβάνει, δίδωσι(ν), φέρει, ἔρχεται/ἀπέρχεται, λέγει, ἀκούει.
- Simple questions and requests: τί; ποῦ; τίς; δός μοι; οὐ/μή for gentle negation.
- Prepositions in clear contexts: ἐν, ἐκ, πρός, ὑπό, μετά. Keep sentences short and pattern‑friendly for comprehensible input.

Visual design
- Species: crow; sleek silhouette, wedge tail, strong straight beak.
- Color: glossy black with blue‑violet sheen; bright highlight on feathers; dark eyes with a lively catch‑light.
- Expressions: big eye shapes, head tilt, raised hackles when excited; wings half‑open to show intention, not threat.
- Scale: roughly the height of a child character from ground to knee when perched on a low fence or stump.
- Props: shiny button, spoon, marble, ribbon; never sharp/dangerous objects.

Staging and camera (children-first perspective)
- Always stage from low to the ground, as seen by a 4‑year‑old.
- Adults appear only from elbows down (hands shoo gently, offer food, or trade items). Never show adult heads.
- Place Korax on low branches, fence posts, or the ground so he reads clearly at child-eye level.
- Use repeated visual beats: the hollow stump by the creek as his stash; a familiar low branch as his lookout.

Boundaries and tone
- Keep stakes cozy and reversible: misplaced, not destroyed; startled, not terrified.
- No cruelty or harm to smaller animals; no mean pranks that cause injury; no ominous omens.
- Ancient Greeks once saw crows as unlucky; here, Korax is mischievous, not evil. He belongs to the woodland community.

Relationships
- With the children: wary fascination becomes playful negotiation (trade and talk). They model asking, waiting, and offering choices.
- With adults: firm but gentle redirection shown by hands/arms only.

Growth arc (across books)
- Early: snatches and runs; returns items only when cornered or tempted.
- Middle: expects trades; begins to ask first and to show finds rather than hide them.
- Later: helps solve problems (guides friends to his stash, fetches, alerts others) while keeping his cheeky pride.

Story seeds
- The Spoon Swap: Korax takes a wooden spoon; a simple trade sequence teaches δίδωσι/λαμβάνει.
- The Shiny Button: he hoards a button, then shares it to cheer a sad friend.
- The Loud Morning: κρα, κρα! wakes everyone; he learns quiet/wait and brings a gift.
- The Lost Ring: he reveals his hollow‑stump stash to help, then receives a ribbon as thanks.

Continuity notes
- Name always Korax (Κόραξ); species always crow (not raven).
- Recurring locations: hollow stump by the creek; low branch near the red gate; small fence post by the path.
- Recurring sound text: κρα, κρα!; occasional echo of last spoken word for fun repetition.

Use Korax to spark questions, trades, and kindness. He is a safe, funny “enemy” whose mischief creates chances to practice core Koine patterns and to show gentle problem‑solving.
